"very unexpected" lost its intensifier (now just "unexpected").
replacement: The Americans advance enormously in productive industry because every one of them throws himself into it at the same time. For that very reason they face very unexpected and formidable troubles. Everyone is in commerce, so their commercial affairs depend on causes too varied and tangled for anyone to predict what trouble may come. Everyone is more or less in productive industry, so at the slightest jolt to business every private fortune is endangered at once, and the state itself is shaken. I believe that these recurring commercial panics are a disease native to the democratic nations of our age. It can be made less dangerous, but it cannot be cured, since it springs not from accidents but from the temperament of these nations.
